title: Village Festival
text: And so… during our pilgrimage, the circus caravan arrived at the eastern village located at the foot of the mountain where Rival's parent dwelled, I say. Apparently slave trading wasn't normally conducted here, but a small-scale event was being held as a detour, for charitable purposes or some such thing. Incidentally, while there was a possibility of Rival's parent appearing, this was said to be one of the trade routes within Melromarc with a fair amount of foot traffic. It was a village full of greedy folk, but from what I understood, that greed wouldn't manifest unless Ren went and slew Rival's parent. If anything, it was recognized as a village that was wicked at heart but outwardly mild-mannered.
“Um… since demi-humans occasionally visit this area, I think the performances don't need to be completely Melromarc-style.”

Father seemed to be organizing everyone's performance content while checking the faith distribution map of the country that he'd received from Lazy Pig. Of course, we had already greeted the eastern village's chief and obtained permission to hold the circus there, indeed. The village itself had grown livelier with the circus's arrival, apparently. On top of that, they were trying to hold a festival to dispel the gloomy atmosphere caused by the Waves. Sometimes villages would piggyback on a circus visit to hold a festival of their own. A “let's have fun especially at times like these” kind of spirit, I suppose. What we needed to be careful of was making sure Ren didn't decide to go hunt down Rival's parent out of sheer boredom. Even the Filolial-samas seemed a bit on edge, sensing a dragon's presence in the wind coming down from the mountain.
“Ren, you mustn't go up the mountain, you know? If you carelessly slay the dragon, it could cause a plague, and this village would suffer tremendous casualties, wouldn't it?”
It seemed Ren hadn't gone and properly slain Rival's parent here after all, since the village wasn't particularly lively.
“Shut up. Don't order me around.”
Ren was being defiant, indeed. If he looked like he might carelessly go off to slay the dragon, I'd stop him without question. This time too, it'd be Sleep Lance.
“Luna-chan, if Ren tries to head for the mountain, feel free to do as you like.”
“Got it—”
“Oi! Don't do anything stupid! Ugh… fine, I won't go, I won't go!”

Leaving Ren to Luna-chan seemed like the way to go. Incidentally, Ren and Keel's performances were limited to once per town or village per day. If the location changed, they could perform again. Since the circus's stay in each location lasted only a few days before moving to the next town or village, repeat performances did happen. But in the eastern village, the likelihood seemed low. Anyway… as long as we stayed away from the mountain, we'd be safe. A village without much character, I say.
“Ohh, circus again today! Big Bro! What should I do?”
“Umm…”

So Father was looking back and forth between Keel and Mole. Mole, too, was gradually settling down under Father's care, apparently. Incidentally, we were also searching for Mole's kin who were being sold as slaves, on the side.
“Keel-kun, let's see… I think it'd be good if you just played with Imiya-chan. Let's go see Raphtalia-chan and the others later too, okay?”
“Alright! Sword Bro, if you're free, wanna play too?”
“I'm not free!”
“Then Luna will take the cute ones out somewhere—somewhere that's not the mountain!”
Luna-chan was requesting an outing with Keel and Ren and the others. It seemed she went out with them from time to time.
“I've already done plenty of hunting today, so it's fine.”

Luna-chan and Keel had gone out with Ren and met back up near this village. So Ren's desires had apparently been satisfied. More importantly, Éclair and Ren seemed to have been training together lately. It started when Éclair invited the lonely Ren to train with her, apparently. She and Crocodile Guy seemed to be fellow curmudgeons, occasionally throwing themselves silently into training together. To be precise, it looked more like Crocodile Guy was casting sympathetic glances at Ren. Depending on the loop, they'd seemed to be on bad terms, so was it surprising that they got along after all? While exchanging such banter, Keel led Ren, Mole, and Luna-chan off to play behind the tent under construction. Of course, the Filolial-samas joined in on that circle of play as well. Elephant was watching over them from a guardian's distance too.
“Wow… looks fun.”
“Let us join, let us join—”
“Sure! Everyone, let's play!”
“Wahh, this kid's so cute—wanna eat some dried meat?”
“Oh? You're giving me some? Thanks!”
“I don't want any! Don't try to feed me!”
“Sword Bro, come on, isn't it fine? Let's eat together.”
“Oi, Keel! Do you understand? Right now we're being treated like dogs!”
The village children, drawn in by the festive atmosphere, joined in the play with Keel and the Filolial-samas, and in the process, Keel and Ren seemed to be getting fed treats.
“Kids can become friends anywhere, huh.”
If the plague had spread, I felt like this village's children would have been drastically reduced in number. In a village steeped in greed, it's always the weak who fall first, I suppose.
“…If only humans and demi-humans could get along regardless of such things…”
Éclair was watching the children playing happily with Crocodile Guy alongside Father and the others.
“Especially Keel-kun—he's good at that sort of thing, so having him around regardless of the performance schedule will be a real help down the road.”
“Indeed…”

Certainly, Keel could talk to anyone without hesitation, so he was well-suited to being a vendor too. And so the circus preparations proceeded without a hitch, and the village steeped itself deeper in festival atmosphere. Surrounding villages, hearing that a circus had come, gathered as well, so things had grown quite lively. Of course, the circus was a great success. It would have been nice if things had gone smoothly in the eastern village without incident, but… I had absolutely no way of predicting that a certain incident would occur here. It happened on a night when the circus and festival were going along nicely.
“Big Bro, Big Bro, something terrible's happened!”
Keel came running up to Father, who had been discussing with the children and the Filolial-samas about touring the village festival after the performance wrapped up, as a sort of celebration.
“What's wrong, Keel-kun?”
“One of the kids I was playing with got snatched by a monster!”
“What!?”
Everyone present set off together, led by Keel.
“Bwoi.”

I saw Lazy Pig plodding listlessly toward the village representative, voice utterly devoid of motivation. No doubt she intended to volunteer herself for the reporting squad rather than the search squad. And so, the place Keel led us to was the outskirts of the village.
“Oi. If we don't chase after them quickly, it'll be dangerous.”
“But Ama, you were told not to go to the mountain.”
“This isn't that kind of situation! A child's life is on the line!”
Ren was being held back by Luna-chan.
“Ren, what's going on?”
“Naofumi, Motoyasu and the others too—hadn't you heard from Keel? A child got snatched by a monster. We should hurry and go rescue them.”
“The circus wrapped up for the day, right? Everyone was starting to head home, and then a girl wandered outside the village, and a monster showed up and dragged her off.”
“That's a situation where every second counts.”
“But we were told not to go to the mountain, and the Filolials keep going on about how it smells like dragon, so they said we should check with you guys first.”

Proper reporting and consultation—that's important, indeed. Still… a village child snatched by a monster was quite the dangerous story. Incidentally, Elephant and the others had been separated from the children in order to participate in the performance.
“Hmm… in games and such, this feels like it'd be a classic event, wouldn't it?”
“True. But this isn't that kind of situation!”

Ren agreed with Father's muttering. And, naturally, there was Rafumi standing right there. You—aren't you sensing something? It felt to me like she was watching the situation unfold without saying a word. But I figured poking at it carelessly here might just stir things up worse, so I decided not to worry about it.
“Human life can't be traded for anything, huh. Alright, let's hurry and rescue the child. Motoyasu-kun.”
“Understood! That said, there's a limit to how far I can go here, so caution is advised, I say.”
“Is something wrong?”
“Well, you see… if I make some careless move, there's a chance I'll gain an even more formidable natural enemy than Rafumi, indeed.”

If at all possible, I wanted to avoid running into Rival. Above all, this was a mountain where dragons lived—if I carelessly got near some stray egg and Rival ended up possessing it, that would be more than I could bear.
“Seems like this is a tough spot for Motoyasu-kun to operate in too… anyway, everyone! Let's split up and search for the child!”
“Um, excuse me”
Separately from Keel, Mole timidly spoke up to Father.
“Imiya-chan, wait here, it'll be fine.”
“Y-yes.”

Father crouched down and smiled at the worried Mole. Mole had only joined recently, after all, and wasn't strengthened enough yet. But… certainly, thinking about it again, there was no mistaking the resemblance to a younger Big Sister. Since present-day Big Sister was young too, being together with her made her reactions to Father recognizable as the same. And so, all of us set off en masse toward the mountain.
